text:
maria: Quick question — noticed a handful of requests where API keys issued via API-Exchange arrived without a project claim and our routing falls back to the org default. That makes per-project quota and rollout dashboards noisy. Should we change the fallback behavior?

sam: Can you paste a minimal example of the request/token so we can reproduce?

maria: Sure — sanitized example:
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi...
claims: {\"org\": \"redwood-org\"}
# no project claim
```
This ends up billed to org-default and shows as "unknown project" in console.

li: That explains the spike we saw in the rollout dashboard — rules that target projects didn't trigger because project was unset.

alex: We discussed similar cases before. Options: (A) attribute to org default project, (B) try to infer from service-account binding (if SA has exactly one project), or (C) reject with a migration 4xx and instruct clients to exchange for a project-scoped token.

sam: I lean toward B (inference) but only if the inference is conservative and instrumented. We don't want silent misattribution of quota.

ops-bot: [audit] token-introspect returned missing project claim at 2024-11-12T16:23:10Z for key id: key_abc123

maria: Proposal: implement heuristic — if issuer == API-Exchange and the SA associated with the key is bound to exactly one project, set project = that project at routing time. Otherwise fall back to org-default. Always emit a telemetry event `auth.project.fallback` with reason tags: `no_claim`, `multiple_projects`, `cross_org`.

li: +1 for heuristic but we need sampling and a console surface that surfaces fallback counts per key and per issuer so SRE/product can triage. Right now those spikes are invisible until customers complain.

alex: UX suggestion: in key detail page show a small banner when fallbacks are detected: "Project inferred via fallback — please confirm mapping" with a Confirm button. If not confirmed after N days, clear the inferred mapping and send a warning. That helps with long-lived accidental attributions.

sam: Add guard: do not infer across org boundaries. If token_org != issuer_org, do not attempt inference (deny or org fallback depending on policy). Also add a canary rollout: enable heuristic for 5% of traffic, emit events, check FP rate.

maria: Sounds good. I'll draft an RFC and a canary plan: 5% traffic, auto-revert if false-positive rate > 2% within 24 hours. Any blockers?

li: No blockers. We also need a test in the quota sim harness to validate accounting changes.

alex: I'll own the canary runbook and console flag. Assigning: @sam telemetry/events, @li console UI, @maria RFC + rollout.

sam: I'll add event names and payloads: `auth.project.fallback` (fields: key_id, issuer, reason, inferred_project?, confirmed_flag), `auth.project.infer_confirmed`, `auth.project.infer_reverted`. Will ensure events include sampling flags.

ops-bot: [deploy] rollout plan created: #canary-auth-fallback (pr-4823) by alex at 2024-11-12T16:40:00Z

maria: Thanks — I'll start the RFC and include a QA checklist: introspect logs, quota accounting diff, console banner tests, and migration guidance for SDKs.

alex: One more note — when we emit telemetry, add a trace/span id so we can link a request to logs for fast triage.

sam: Good call. I'll add tracing fields to the event schema.

li: :thumbsup: let's sync tomorrow for the canary timeline and dashboard queries we need.

maria: Done for now, will ping when RFC is ready for review.
